references.text: God identifies himself as the Lord who brought Israel out of Egypt, from the house of bondage—the same self-identification found in Leviticus 26:13.
God promises to free Israel from forced labor in Egypt and release them from slavery—the fulfillment of this is described in Leviticus 26:13.
Repeats God's self-presentation as the one who led the people out of Egypt, from the house of bondage.
The prophet Isaiah uses the image of breaking the yoke and the staff of the oppressor, employing the same imagery found in Leviticus 26:13.
God reminds that he broke Israel's yoke and loosened their bonds—the same metaphor of liberation.
Ezekiel uses the same expression about breaking the bars of the yoke and freeing the people from slavery.
Refers to the deliverance from Egypt when Israel was young—the same historical event.
Jesus proclaims freedom for captives and the oppressed—a spiritual fulfillment of the liberation described in Leviticus 26:13.
Paul urges believers to stand firm in the freedom Christ has set them free to, and not again submit to the yoke of slavery.
Creation itself will be liberated from bondage under decay—the theme of deliverance from slavery.
